minutes.headline: Sewer Commission sent a Chestnut Street sewer-area expansion to the Apr 13 agenda and denied a toilet-leak credit.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a developer's engineer ask to bring the back land at 5 Chestnut Street into the sewer service area ahead of a May 1 Town Meeting petition. Members split on whether it enables a roughly 40-unit development; no vote was taken and the capacity review was assigned to the staff engineer. The board also declined a bill adjustment for a toilet leak, took up a hardship request from a well customer on a flat charge, and agreed to draft a new well-customer policy. It approved a corrected quarterly commitment, the Q3 commitment and the prior minutes, and heard updates on Elizabeth Street inflow and infiltration.

budget_items.what_was_said: Staff gave the per-100-cubic-feet cost the town pays Leominster to compare against what customers are charged.
Well customers pay a flat quarterly charge set from old averages, while the metered minimum is much lower. A 90-year-old customer asked to pay the minimum instead.
Members estimated a well meter, plumber and permit would cost several hundred dollars to over a thousand, paying back within about a year.
The commitment was mistyped and raised by ten thousand, then re-voted.

what_happened.line: The commission heard a developer's engineer ask to bring the back land at 5 Chestnut Street into the sewer service area; no vote was taken and the staff engineer will review capacity.
The Chestnut Street item was set to return on the April 13 agenda.
The commission voted to make no adjustment to the sewer bill for a toilet leak at 183 Whalen Road; the vote tally was not audible.
A flat-charge hardship request from a well customer led to a plan to put a new well-customer rate policy on the next agenda.
Members re-voted a corrected Q1 FY21 commitment, approved the Q3 commitment and the prior minutes, and set the next meetings for April 13 and April 27.

why_it_matters: Bringing more land into the sewer service area can change how much of the system's capacity is committed, which is why the capacity review comes before the May 1 Town Meeting petition.
Well customers pay a flat quarterly charge, and a new policy could change what they pay compared with metered customers.
The commission noted it has had to borrow from retained earnings, so billing decisions and grant efforts bear on sewer rates.
watch_next: April 13 meeting: the Chestnut Street expansion returns with the staff engineer's capacity review, and a well-customer policy may be on the agenda.
May 1 Town Meeting: the petition to extend the sewer service area at 5 Chestnut Street.
